THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners who are arraigned as accused Nos.2 & 3 have filed this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest in Jnanabharathi Police Station Cr.No.65/2024, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 306 & 498A r/w Section 34 of the IPC.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned HCGP.
Perused the records.
3. As per the case of the prosecution, accused No.1, who is brother of petitioner No.1/accused No.2 got married with deceased and it was a love marriage and the marriage was subsequently registered.
Initially, accused No.1 was residing with petitioners, but after the marriage, they started to residing in rented house in Ullal road within the limits of Jnanabharathi Police Station, Bengaluru.

Initially,
they lead happy married life and subsequently, accused No.1 under the influence of alcohol used to NC: 2024:KHC:14615 physically & mentally harass the deceased and it is alleged that the present petitioners used to intervene in their family affairs and have instigated.
It is also alleged that being unable to tolerate the ill-treatment by accused No.1, on 14.02.2024 at 7.30 a.m., the deceased is said to have committed suicide by consuming some tablets.
In this regard, a complaint was lodged and on the basis of the complaint, crime came to be registered.
Apprehending the arrest, the petitioners have approached the learned Sessions Judge and the learned Sessions Judge has rejected their bail petition.
Hence, they are before this Court.
4. The allegations made in the complaint clearly disclose that the petitioners were residing separately from accused No.1 and deceased.

The only allegation made against the present petitioners are that they used to intervene in the family affairs of deceased and they used to instigate her asserting that she does not know cooking and she was not taught anything in this regard by her NC:
2024:KHC:14615 family members and they would perform the second marriage of accused No.1.
But whether these assertions attract the ingredients of the offence under Section 306 of IPC is required to be considered.
5. To prosecute for offence under Section 306 of IPC, the ingredients of Section 107 of IPC are required to be established by the prosecution.

In the instant case, the allegations were made against accused No.1 regarding physical and mental harassment, but as against the present petitioner, it is simply asserted that they used to humiliate the deceased.
Whether that amounts to instigation is a question mark and prima facie on perusing the records it is evident that they are residing separately.

sentences.text:
The petitioners are not directly concerned with the family affairs of deceased &
accused No.1.
It is also submitted that accused No.1 was already arrested and subsequently was enlarged on bail.
Considering these facts & circumstances, I do not find any impediment for admitting the petitioners on anticipatory bail.
The other apprehensions raised by the learned HCGP can be meted out by imposing certain conditions.

Hence, the petition needs to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER I.
The petition is allowed.

II. The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest in Cr.No.65/2024 of Jnanabharathi Police station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 306 & 498A r/w Section 34 of the IPC pending on the file of IX Additional C.M.M. Court, Nrupatunga Road, Bangalore on each executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with one surety each for like-sum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer or the concerned trial Court, subject to following conditions:

(i) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 & 3 shall surrender themselves before the Investigating Officer within fifteen days from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order and in the event of NC: 2024:KHC:14615 their surrender, Investigating Officer/SHO shall release them on bail as directed.
(ii) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 & 3 shall not directly or indirectly tamper with any of the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 & 3 shall not indulge in any similar offences.
(iv) Petitioners/accused Nos.2 & 3 shall make themselves available to the Investigating Officer for interrogation whenever called for during course of investigation.

(v) Petitioner No.2/accused No.3 shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer/SHO between 9.00 a.m. and 5.00 p.m. on every first Saturday of the month till the final report is submitted.
